fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Clear an open staging area near the driveway entrance where responding units can park without blocking the access drive.
• Mark the access drive entrance with posts or reflectors to define its edges, particularly where dense vegetation narrows the visible opening.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move freely between the two buildings.
• Keep a gate or opening in any fencing along the rear of the property unlocked and clearly marked to allow responders to reach the rear on foot when vehicle access is not possible.
• Trim shrubs and low tree branches along the walkway so responders can move quickly along it without obstruction.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored materials so it can be used as a secondary staging area if needed.
• Post a visible sign or marker near the detached structure identifying it as a separate building so arriving responders can account for it without searching the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Brush Area; Mixed Vegetation; Open Terrain; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Ground Vegetation; Multiple Access Routes; Large Trees; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on large trees that hang directly over or touch the house or other structures.
• Thin shrubs growing close to the walls of the structure to create open space between the plants and the building.
• Remove or cut back brush in the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Clear ground vegetation growing against the base of the structure.
• Keep the area beneath large trees free of shrubs and brush that could carry fire up into the tree canopy.
• Separate clusters of shrubs growing near the structure so they are not touching each other or the building.
• Cut back any brush or overhanging branches along driveways to keep both access routes open and passable.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from around the base of trees and shrubs near the structure.
• Maintain open ground between the scattered trees and any shrub patches near the structure.
